title: Odd Symmetry of f(x) = x + 1/x
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether the function p(x) = x + 1/x is even, odd, or neither, and describe the symmetry this imposes on its graph.
finalAnswer: \text{odd: } p(-x) = -p(x); \text{ the graph is symmetric about the origin}

steps.title: Confirm the Domain is Symmetric
steps.explanation: The reciprocal term excludes only x = 0, and the remaining set is unchanged when x is replaced by -x, a necessary precondition for any parity test.
steps.why: Evenness or oddness can only be discussed for functions whose domain comes in +/- pairs; p fails only at the single point 0.

steps.title: Evaluate p at -x
steps.explanation: Substituting -x into both terms gives the negation of x and the reciprocal of -x, which is -1/x.
steps.why: Reciprocation preserves sign structure: 1/(-x) = -(1/x), so both summands flip simultaneously.

steps.title: Compare with -p(x)
steps.explanation: Distributing the minus sign through p reproduces exactly the expression found for p(-x), establishing the oddness identity.
steps.why: The defining test for an odd function is p(-x) = -p(x) for every domain point, and both sides match term by term.

steps.title: Read Off the Geometric Symmetry
steps.explanation: Oddness means every point of the graph has a partner obtained by a half-turn about the origin, so the curve is origin-symmetric.
steps.why: Reflecting through the origin negates both coordinates; the identity p(-x) = -p(x) guarantees the reflected point still satisfies y = p(x).
